question: Why do America's poorest people live years longer in some cities than in others?
answer: Mostly because of local habits and surroundings, not medical care. Chetty and colleagues found the poorest quarter's life expectancy varied by about 4.5 years between areas, tracking smoking, obesity and exercise, and living among richer, better-educated neighbours. It barely tracked access to doctors. A poor New Yorker tends to outlive a poor Detroiter.
move: The habits around you shape your health more than the clinic down the road.
ask: Which habits of the people I spend most time with am I slowly picking up, for better or worse?
reference: Chetty et al., The association between income and life expectancy in the United States, 2001-2014, JAMA, 2016
